findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. A first-time reader can repeat it back after one read.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The page says why it exists: it is a study of firstmate that shows what Athena can do. Without this, a newcomer would wonder why a page about Athena is mostly about another tool.
findings.source: "A study is Athena's written reading of another software project, taken at one fixed commit... Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it"

findings.text: The first section after the header is a failure message. It shows none of the models, verdict or costs the opening promises, which weakens a newcomer's first impression of the key selling point.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: This link in the header is meant for the project owner. A newcomer is not told what these proposals are or whether the link concerns them.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: What to do next is easy to find and concrete. There is a link to jump there, the requirements are listed (git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, Claude Code or npm), and the clone, `./setup.sh` and `athena ask "add a changelog"` commands are given in order.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the Next steps section

findings.text: The main body is dense: 12 transition cards, 6 design-choice cards and 45 claims, with long, overlapping sentences. A newcomer who only wants to understand Athena will likely skim or stop here.
findings.source: Transitions section, e.g. t4 Guard: "worktree clean and committed work landed, whether the captain approved the merge, firstmate merged it under yolo, or a local-only ship landed by a guarded fast-forward; a local-only project also counts work merged into the local default branch..."

findings.text: Several glossary entries say that the term is undefined instead of defining it. This is honest, but the reader is left with a few key words they cannot pin down.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a captain call." (also durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake)

findings.text: The Start here section is well built: the words are defined before they are used, then come a plain summary, a step-by-step walk-through and the failure cases. A reader who wants firstmate's details can follow them.
findings.source: Start here: "The three parts below say what firstmate is, follow one piece of work, and say what happens when something fails or has no limit."

findings.text: This refers to Athena's internal folder layout without saying where that folder lives. A newcomer gets nothing they can act on from it.
findings.source: About this page: "This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
